episodes.163345: A strong cold front produced squalls that resulted in gale- to storm-force wind gusts.
episodes.163606: Instability caused by an upper air disturbance triggered heavy showers over portions of the Big Island and Maui.  The precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious property damage or injuries were reported.
episodes.163758: A mid-upper level disturbance across the FL Straits continued to push northward towards South FL which allowed for a deepening moist layer across the Florida east coast. This favored widespread showers and thunderstorms with gusty wind, heavy rainfall, and flooding.
episodes.164006: A cold front in mid-November interacted with a trough over the Mexican Plateau, as well as above normal temperatures, to create numerous showers and storms across the populated Lower Rio Grande Valley extending into Brooks County.  Heaviest rains, estimated at 4 to 5 inches, fell along the Rio Grande southeast of Brownsville; over 2 inches in less than 2 hours created localized urban flooding in the city.
episodes.164007: Gusty showers and thunderstorms, associated with a cold front, moved offshore early in the afternoon on November 18th. Some of these thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts that were recorded at some of the marine observing platforms along the coast between Port Mansfield and the mouth of the Rio Grande.
episodes.164209: A low pressure system tracking north of Lake Superior produced west storm force gusts at Stannard Rock early on the 18th.

events.narrative: The Texas Coastal Ocean Observing Network (TCOON) site at Realitos Peninsula (RLIT2) reported a 35 knot (40 mph) wind gust associated with the strong thunderstorms moving eastward across the region at 11:54 AM CST. There were several gusts of 34 knots (39 mph) between 11:54 AM CST and 12:42 PM CST.

Several gusts of 34 knots (39 mph) or greater were reported between 12:42 PM CST and 2:00 PM CST.

events.county: Laguna Madre From Port Of Brownsville To Arroyo Colorado
events.narrative: The Port Isabel Water Level Observation Network (PTIT2) reported a 34 knot (39 mph) wind gust associated with the strong thunderstorms moving eastward across the region at 1:00 PM and 1:24 PM CST.

Torrential rains of 1.5 to 2 inches in one hour reported, and more than 2 inches in less than 2 hours,  at Brownsville/South Padre International Airport and nearby neighborhoods in Cameron County caused flooding at the intersection of Boca Chica and Highway 48. Local Emergency Manager reported waters flowing over the curb and the intersection becoming impassable at 1:28 PM.

Various broadcast media outlets and members of the public reported significant flooding across the downtown and midtown areas of Miami. Significant flooding of roadways with stalled vehicles in the flood waters along the Biscayne Boulevard corridor from NE 15th Street to NE 9th Street. Rainfall measurements from nearby rain gauges was around 3 inches, most of which fell in a very short period of time.

Various broadcast media outlets and members of the public reported flooding across portions of Miami Beach. Flooding near the intersection of Alton Road and 10th Street with several inches of standing water over the curb, sidewalk, and roadway and water halfway up car tires, flooding near the intersection of Collins Avenue and 36th Street with several inches of water above the roadway and sidewalk and halfway up car tires, significant flooding near the intersection of 34th Street and Collins Avenue with water entering a building, and flooding near 5th Street and Michigan Avenue with standing water on the roadway and sidewalks with curbs completely under water and water more than halfway up car tires. Rainfall estimates were around 3 inches, most of which fell in a very short period of time.
